transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, with Liam our solutions engineer and Zoe from customer success. Can you hear us ok?
[00:06] Jared Kim: Yup, loud and clear. Sorry, brief background - we are Lumasearch, building an enterprise search product, heavy on docs, a lot of long form content. We're evaluating vector search, trying to improve relevance.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Great, that matches what Priya told me. Today we'll walk through our hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints, show a demo of a sample query flow, and talk tradeoffs for latency and cost. We'll try to keep it concrete.
[00:29] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Key constraints for us: 100k monthly active queries, 200M docs, must keep p95 query latency under 250ms in the UI, and security requirements - SOC2, KMS, and audit logs.
[00:41] Liam O'Connor: Perfect, we'll address those. Quick agenda: 1) show embeddings API, model choices and indexing tips; 2) retrieval + rerank patterns; 3) demo with live queries; 4) Q&A and next steps.
[00:55] Maya Patel: Quick note: today's demo uses our hosted API - we can talk Dedicated or Private later if you need VPC/KMS inside your cloud.
[01:03] Marco Reyes: For us VPC is a maybe; initially we want hosted but keys and retention controls are must-haves.
[01:10] Zoe Chen: Noted - we'll follow up with the security pack.
[01:13] Liam O'Connor: Ok diving in - embeddings. Redwood exposes a embeddings endpoint: you POST documents or text and get back vectors. We support multiple model variants - smaller dims for cheaper and faster indexing, and higher-dim models for quality. Typical dims we see are 1536 and 4096 depending on model.
[01:28] Priya Singh: Do you expose the raw float vectors or quantized? How do you handle storage?
[01:33] Liam O'Connor: Hosted returns float vectors in the response; storage on Redwood side is managed and uses vector indexes - for Hosted we use compressed storage with quantization under the hood for cost. For Dedicated we give more control and you can bring your FAISS index if you want. There may be small differences in exact precision, which occasionally affects edge-case recall.
[01:50] Jared Kim: If we want deterministic exactness, is Dedicated the only option?
[01:53] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated gives you pinned kernels and more deterministic quantization options. Hosted is optimized for economic majority of workloads and still very high quality.
[02:01] [02:01] Maya Patel: Quick demo now - Liam will share his screen and walk through code snippets for both the retrieve+rerank pattern and single-step rerank.
[02:09] Liam O'Connor: (screen) Alright, here's a sample flow. Step 1: call /embeddings with a batch of documents to index, we show response vectors. Step 2: index into your vector DB - with Hosted you can use our managed index or export vectors to your FAISS cluster. Step 3: on query, use k-NN to get top 100 candidates, then call Redwood /rerank with the question + candidate passages - rerank returns a scored list.
[02:33] Priya Singh: So rerank is another API call that takes a list of passages and the query? Latency then is two-hop - retrieval plus rerank. How to keep under 250ms?
[02:43] Liam O'Connor: Good question. Two common patterns: 1) small-k rerank (e.g., top 10) - keep retrieval fast with ANN like HNSW, then rerank 10 passages - fast enough when tuned; 2) hybrid single-call rerank where we include a smaller candidate set or use model variants optimized for latency. Redwood Optimize can recommend top_k and batching to meet your SLO.
[03:02] Marco Reyes: What's your observed p50/p95 for the rerank call for 10 passages on Hosted?
[03:07] Liam O'Connor: For our typical 1536-dim model, hosted rerank for 10 passages is around 35-60ms p50, p95 typically under 200ms in our US regions, depends on text length. If you add network and retrieval it's usually around 120-220ms for the whole retrieve+rerank flow in our benchmarks.
[03:28] Ellen Park: Are there options to do partial rerank in the client to avoid a second API hop?
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: You can do a hybrid approach: do vector similarity offline for the heavy lift and only hit rerank for ambiguous queries, or use a cheaper similarity scoring on top of embeddings for initial ranking. Also caching the top results for frequent queries helps.
[03:47] [03:47] Priya Singh: Can you show the code for calling /rerank?
[03:50] Liam O'Connor: Sure. (types) Example payload: {"query":"how do I reset password","candidates":[{id:1, text:"..."},...], "model":"redwood-rerank-1536"} response comes back with scores and final ranking. We also surface explainability metadata - token overlaps, scores - though it's approximate.
[04:14] Jared Kim: Any limit on candidate list size? We could in theory send 1000 passages, but that seems silly.
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: For Hosted we recommend <=200 candidates; very large lists increase latency and cost. The sweet spot is usually 50-150 for deep re-ranking in heavy-document contexts, but many customers find 10-50 optimal. Redwood Optimize can simulate cost impact.
[04:33] Priya Singh: How does Redwood handle batching and concurrency? We'll have spikes.
[04:37] Liam O'Connor: Hosted has autoscaling and request batching at the runtime level. We do request coalescing when possible. For latency SLOs you can set route policies to favor lower-latency nodes. If you need strict p95 you might move to Dedicated.
[04:51] Marco Reyes: Security - data retention and encryption at rest?
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: Hosted encrypts data at rest; customer data retention policies are configurable, and we provide audit logs. For KMS integrations and keys under your control we recommend Dedicated or our Private offering. We'll share the SOC2 pack.
[05:08] Maya Patel: Quick live example - we're going to run a demo on a small dataset of product docs. You'll see first the embedding index retrieval then rerank.
[05:16] [05:16] (demo noise, screen share)
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: Running query: "how to optimize search relevance for long documents" - retrieving top 100 via ANN, scoring, then rerank top 15.
[05:32] (typing sounds)
[05:35] Liam O'Connor: Results: top doc about semantic chunking got highest rerank score. You can see the rerank scores per passage and the final sorted order.
[05:44] Priya Singh: I like the explainability table. We need to see how those scores align with our label data. Can we export rerank logs?
[05:52] Zoe Chen: Yes, we can stream logs to S3 or to your cloud bucket for offline evaluation; we'll include retention controls.
[05:59] Jared Kim: What about vector export for experimentation with our FAISS setup?
[06:04] Liam O'Connor: You can export vectors via the API or use our managed index and snapshot exports. For Dedicated you get full control over index storage.
[06:13] [06:13] Priya Singh: Cost question: per-call rerank cost looks expensive if we do rerank on every query. Any recommendations?
[06:18] Maya Patel: Good point. Typical recommendations: 1) do a fast filter first (keyword or cheap vector similarity) and only rerank top-N; 2) use lower-dim models for retrieval and higher-dim for rerank; 3) cache frequent results; 4) Redwood Optimize will suggest top_k and model mixes to hit a cost target. We'll include a cost modeling spreadsheet.
[06:41] Marco Reyes: For our traffic shape, caching will help. We have a lot of repeated queries.
[06:45] Liam O'Connor: Also we've got prefix caching and KV cache for model context to speed up repeated calls.
[06:50] Ellen Park: How do we measure recall/quality?
[06:53] Liam O'Connor: We recommend a small eval set of labeled queries. Run bench tests with different top_k and rerank thresholds; Redwood has evaluation tooling to track regressions and quality metrics. We can run a small benchmark for you if you share sample labels.
[07:07] Priya Singh: We'll share a 200-query labeled set.
[07:10] Maya Patel: Great.
[07:13] Jared Kim: Any multi-region support? We have users in EU and US, want data residency in EU for some customers.
[07:19] Liam O'Connor: Hosted supports regional endpoints; for strict data residency we recommend Private or Dedicated in your region. Hosted can restrict where data is stored for enterprise customers with contracts. We'll flag that for legal.
[07:31] Priya Singh: We also need SAML/SSO for team access.
[07:34] Zoe Chen: Redwood supports SSO, RBAC, and audit logs - we'll attach the SSO flow doc.
[07:40] Maya Patel: Ok quick architecture slide: client UI -> query -> call Redwood embeddings+vector retrieval -> rerank endpoint -> UI. We also show optional step: use managed index vs export.
[07:52] Liam O'Connor: Another nuance - for very long documents chunking strategy matters. We recommend semantic chunking to keep passages coherent and reduce noise. That impacts recall.
[08:03] Priya Singh: How does Redwood handle dynamic content updates? Our docs change frequently.
[08:07] Liam O'Connor: We support incremental indexing; you can upsert vectors. For heavy write workloads we recommend batch uploads during low-traffic windows. There's also background compaction for indexes.
[08:18] Jared Kim: Any limits on concurrent upserts?
[08:21] Liam O'Connor: Hosted handles high concurrency but you'll want to throttle to avoid index rebalancing spikes; we'll share best-practice patterns.
[08:31] [08:31] Priya Singh: Show the SDK snippet for embeddings?
[08:34] Liam O'Connor: (types) Example: client.embeddings.create({model:"redwood-embed-1536", input:["text1","text2"]}) returns vectors array. For batching we recommend 100–500 texts depending on doc size.
[08:47] Marco Reyes: What about per-request size limits?
[08:50] Liam O'Connor: Payload limits are documented - roughly 10k tokens per call for generation endpoints; for embeddings we recommend chunking if text is >3k tokens. Large payloads increase latency and cost.
[09:02] Ellen Park: Do you provide a hosted search UI or connectors?
[09:05] Maya Patel: We provide sample connectors and reference apps; customers often integrate with their own UI. We can share the repo.
[09:12] Jared Kim: Can you run a small end-to-end benchmark with our sample dataset?
[09:16] Maya Patel: Yes - next step we'll run a benchmark on your 200-query labeled set and share precision/recall and cost estimates.
[09:23] Priya Singh: Timeline: we want a POC in the next three weeks.
[09:26] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. We'll scope a 4-week POC: ingest sample dataset, run benchmarks, tune top_k, and deliver a results dashboard.
[09:34] Marco Reyes: Curious about throttling and quotas during POC - will we hit rate limits?
[09:38] Zoe Chen: We'll provision a trial key with increased limits for the POC; will coordinate with infra.
[09:43] [09:43] Jared Kim: Any gotchas?
[09:45] Liam O'Connor: A few: 1) chunking strategy can make or break relevance; 2) mixing dims across retrieval/rerank needs testing; 3) edge-case tokens or OCR'd text require cleanup; 4) network egress for export might add cost.
[09:59] Priya Singh: Good list.
[10:01] Maya Patel: Ok final Q&A - Priya, Jared?
[10:05] Priya Singh: Will you share the performance spreadsheets and cost model?
[10:07] Maya Patel: Yes, I'll send the pricing and a cost modeling sheet after the call.
[10:11] Jared Kim: Who will be our point of contact?
[10:13] Maya Patel: I'll be primary for contract/pricing, Liam is SE for technical follow-up, Zoe will manage POC logistics.
[10:21] (brief crosstalk)
[10:25] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs. End of demo.
